18                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

19   Resolution Number 1523, by Senator Seward, 

20   congratulating the Cooperstown Central School 

21   Girls Basketball Team upon the occasion of 

22   capturing the New York State Class C 

23   championship.

24                "WHEREAS, Excellence and success in 

25   competitive sports can only be achieved through 


                                                                2149

 1   strenuous practice, team play, and team spirit, 

 2   nurtured by dedicated coaching and strategic 

 3   planning; and 

 4                "WHEREAS, It is the intent of this 

 5   Legislative Body to recognize those young people 

 6   within our community who, by achieving 

 7   outstanding success in athletic competitions, 

 8   have inspired and brought pride to their school 

 9   district and community; and 

10                "WHEREAS, Attendant to such concern,  

11   and in full accord with its long-standing 

12   traditions, this Legislative Body is justly proud  

13   to congratulate the Cooperstown Central School 

14   Girls Basketball Team upon the occasion of 

15   capturing the New York State Class C Championship  

16   on Sunday, March 22, 2015, at Hudson Valley 

17   Community College in Troy, New York; and 

18                "WHEREAS, The Cooperstown Central 

19   School Hawkeyes won their first Class C 

20   Basketball Championship in school history with an 

21   impressive 61-34 victory over Northern Adirondack 

22   Central School; and 

23                "WHEREAS, The athletic talent 

24   displayed by this team is due in great part to 

25   the efforts of Coach Mike Niles and his team of 


                                                                2150

 1   outstanding assistant coaches, skilled and 

 2   inspirational tutors, respected for their ability 

 3   to develop potential into excellence; and 

 4                "WHEREAS, The team's overall record 

 5   of 25-1 is outstanding, and the team members were  

 6   loyally and enthusiastically supported by family, 

 7   fans, friends and the community at large; and 

 8                "WHEREAS, Athletically and 

 9   academically, the team members have proven 

10   themselves to be an unbeatable combination of 

11   talents, reflecting favorably on their school; 

12   and 

13                "WHEREAS, Sports competition 

14   instills the values of teamwork, pride and 

15   accomplishment, and Coach Mike Niles and his 

16   outstanding athletes have clearly made a 

17   contribution to the spirit of excellence which is 

18   a tradition of their school; now, therefore, be 

19   it 

20                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

21   Body pause in its deliberations to congratulate 

22   the Cooperstown Central School Girls Basketball 

23   Team; its members:  Julie Ford, Christina Noto, 

24   Maggie Schuermann, Meaghan Perrino, Liz Millea, 

25   Mya Murdock, Sam Fanion, Paige Cring, Maria Noto, 


                                                                2151

 1   Sara Fountain, Fiona McGoldrick, Sarah Cook, Jen  

 2   Flynn, Ciara McGoldrick, Sam Wehner, Mallory 

 3   Arthurs, Coach Mike Niles, and Assistant Coaches  

 4   Glen Noto, Matt Hazzard and Shannon Merwin, on 

 5   their outstanding season and overall team record; 

 6   and be it further 

 7                "RESOLVED, That copies of this  

 8   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to 

 9   the members of the Cooperstown Central School 

10   Girls Basketball Team, Coach Mike Niles, and 

11   Assistant Coaches."

12                ACTING PRESIDENT BOYLE:   Senator 

13   Seward.

14                SENATOR SEWARD:   Thank you, 

15   Mr. President.  

16                You know, often when we speak of 

17   Cooperstown, we're talking baseball.  But today, 

18   today we're speaking about high school basketball 

19   in Cooperstown.  

20                You know, I am extremely pleased to 

21   welcome to the State Capitol and specifically our 

22   Senate chamber today the Lady Hawkeyes of 

23   Cooperstown, along with their coach, Mike Niles.  

24   And I know Assistant Coach Glen Noto is along 

25   today as well.  


                                                                2152

 1                These are the 2015 New York State 

 2   High School Class C Girls Basketball Champions.  

 3   You know, this team is truly made up of 

 4   trailblazers, because they brought home the very 

 5   first basketball championship to Cooperstown.  

 6                You know, this winter they put 

 7   together a dominant and very impressive record of 

 8   25 and 1.  And that season concluded with a very 

 9   impressive win over Northern Adirondack to 

10   capture the state championship.  And my apologies 

11   to Senator Betty Little, who represents that 

12   school district.

13                (Laughter.)

14                SENATOR SEWARD:   This is a team 

15   that had a goal in mind and they worked very, 

16   very hard to achieve it.  You know, from those 

17   extra practices at the Clark Sports Center, the 

18   summer tournaments, the late nights at the 

19   Cooperstown High School gymnasium, and I'm 

20   certain in a few neighborhood driveways shooting 

21   hoops at home, they put in the hard work.  And 

22   the result was a much-sought-after state title, 

23   and that was a true crowning achievement for 

24   their efforts.

25                And of course the girls were not 


                                                                2153

 1   alone in their journey.  The guiding hand of 

 2   their coaches, the very loving encouragement of 

 3   parents and family members, and the very 

 4   enthusiastic support of the entire Cooperstown 

 5   community must also be recognized here today.

 6                And along with the success on the 

 7   basketball court, these girls have excelled also 

 8   in the classroom.  They were recently named a 

 9   New York State Public High School Athletic 

10   Association Scholar/Athlete Team, with an 

11   impressive 94.18 GPA.  Truly, they epitomize the 

12   term "student athletes."  

13                They are terrific role models for 

14   other students.  Young basketball players now 

15   look up to them.  And the community at large, I 

16   can tell you, is very, very proud.

17                Now, I don't want to put any 

18   pressure on this great team, but the vast 

19   majority of the team are not seniors and they'll 

20   be coming back next year.  So a fair warning to 

21   the rest of New York State that has Class C 

22   teams:  The Cooperstown Lady Hawkeyes are ready 

23   to repeat in 2016.

24                But today we honor them for their 

25   2015 accomplishments, and I say, on behalf of all 


                                                                2154

 1   of those I'm privileged to represent in our part 

 2   of New York State and on behalf of this entire 

 3   body of the New York State Senate that has 

 4   adopted this resolution, we say congratulations, 

 5   you've done a great job.

 6                (Sustained applause.)

 7                ACTING PRESIDENT BOYLE:   Senator 

 8   DeFrancisco.

 9                SENATOR DeFRANCISCO:   Yes, I just 

10   want to rise and also congratulate you.  

11                Having been involved in playing 

12   sports most of my adult life -- it's getting less 

13   and less every year -- I understand how important 

14   this is to all of you now.  But you won't believe 

15   how it gains in importance over time.  Because 

16   all the friends that you're playing with now and 

17   will be playing with next year and years to come 

18   in different sports, they're going to be your 

19   friends forever.  Forever.  Because you've shared 

20   something that very few people share.  

21                So although the championship is 

22   wonderful, it's something you can be proud of, 

23   it will seem even better in the future when you 

24   meet your old friends and the stories will get 

25   better.  You'll get better -- you'll remember how 


                                                                2155

 1   much better it was and all the things you did 

 2   that maybe you didn't.  

 3                But it's a wonderful thing, and I 

 4   really appreciate it.  And women's basketball is 

 5   really on the rise.  There's a woman that I'm 

 6   sure all of you have heard of that's from my 

 7   district, and that's somebody that plays for 

 8   Connecticut.  Stewart?  She is unbelievable.  

 9   She's won the championship three years in a row, 

10   got one more to go, Most Valuable Player.  

11                So maybe you aren't going to be 

12   6 foot 4 with a 7-foot wingspan, but you can 

13   enjoy that game as much as she can and enjoy your 

14   successes.  Thank you.  

15                (Applause from gallery.)

16                ACTING PRESIDENT BOYLE:   Thank you, 

17   Senator.

18                Congratulations, ladies.

14   Steele, Karina Warren, Paige Weston; Team Manager

25                SENATOR RITCHIE:   Thank you, 


                                                                2159

 1   Mr. President.

 2                I want to welcome the New York State 

 3   Class D Girls Basketball champs here today, the 

 4   Heuvelton Lady Bulldogs.  And they come from my 

 5   home and my alma mater.  

 6                I have to say it's extra special to 

 7   have these girls here, because they're my friends 

 8   and my neighbors.  One of the girls lives down 

 9   the road.  One actually grew up across from my 

10   in-laws.  One is the daughter of my high school 

11   math teacher.  And I could pretty much tell a 

12   story about every girl that's up there.  So for 

13   me personally, it's been really wonderful to 

14   watch how hard you've worked and how far you've 

15   come.  

16                I know, from such a small area, I 

17   think we probably surprised a lot of people when 

18   they saw all the supporters that you had at your 

19   championship game.  And though I couldn't be 

20   there, I was one of the many that sat home 

21   watching the game, yelling "Go, girls, go!"  So 

22   for such a small area to have amassed such a huge 

23   amount of support just goes to the character of 

24   the girls that are on the team.  

25                You know, I saw the championship 


                                                                2160

 1   game where you beat South Kortright by 61-54.  I 

 2   would like to acknowledge the great game that 

 3   Senator Seward's team played too.  It really was 

 4   a wonderful game, and I'm so thrilled to see that 

 5   the Lady Bulldogs won the state championship.  

 6                But I'd also like to just take a 

 7   couple of minutes to talk about the girls 

 8   themselves.  You know, I watched the NCAA 

 9   championship between Kentucky and Wisconsin, and 

10   I was a little disappointed when I saw Kentucky 

11   leave the floor without shaking hands and showing 

12   us, even though it was a tough game, some 

13   sportsmanship.  

14                But I've got to tell you, these 

15   girls up here off the court have shown grace and 

16   humility.  And these girls are what good leaders 

17   of the future are made of.  So I want to say to 

18   all of you, your coaches -- Rob, Austin, I want 

19   to thank you.  Is Dave up there, Dave Steele, the 

20   athletic director?  I want to make sure that all 

21   of you know how proud not just myself but the 

22   entire community are of what you've accomplished, 

23   of the young women that you have become, and I 

24   want to congratulate you on your wonderful 

25   championship.
